name: Music-Synchronized Animation
visualIdentity: A timing method for reveals, cuts, and motion accents keyed to verified beats, downbeats, and musical sections. It can support abstract, illustrated, cinematic, or typographic visuals; the source defines no intrinsic palette or material style.
suitableUses: Explicitly fits product and editorial introductions, explanatory or illustrated narratives, and abstract or cinematic sequences with meaningful chapters. Lyric videos and music videos are suggested combinations. Suitability for interactive HTML is inferred: finite progress can map the same states to scroll.
limitations: Too-short topics may not need chapters. Avoid transitions that obscure causality, unexplained scene changes, or breaks in a continuous-shot or loop requirement. Do not start every element on one beat or remove reading time. Music synchronization supplies timing, not visual construction.
palette: No canonical palette is specified. Preserve task, brand, reference, and existing semantic colors and the selected visual style’s color limits. The optional example is background #F3EBDD, foreground #293B44, accents #628C98 and #BA7B61, with discrete colors and no gradient. The main foreground/background pair has 9.836 contrast; accents are decorative only at 3.174 and 3.379. Check actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Analyze beats, downbeats, sections, and energy; manually verify them and store a shared event table for picture and sound. Vary density, anticipation, pauses, and reading holds. For video, derive every state from seekable composition time. For HTML, scroll may scrub bounded chapter or story progress; backward movement must restore coherent states. Beat mapping and scroll mechanics are distinct.
audio: No fixed genre, tempo, voice, or required audio layer. Honor supplied choices; otherwise propose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience. Use the same timing data for audio and visuals, then check intelligibility, balance, clipping, and sync.
assetRequirements: Use authorized audio and supplied copy or assets; do not assume missing media exists. Precompute beats, onsets, and energy with Python/librosa if useful, manually verify results, and save timestamps. Seed randomness and cache or bake stateful visuals. Inspect fonts, glyphs, crops, and representative frames.
combinations: Needs a visual style. Suggested pairings: style-094 abstract shapes for rhythm, with the primary palette and no same-beat starts; style-093 lyric typography for stressed words, with reading holds. Chapter transitions and narrative progression may suit longer stories; omit when they add no meaning or conflict with continuity.
productionApproach: Choose visual renderer and motion engine from the style, action, assets, and fidelity needs; each owns its layer and each animated property has one owner. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, sync, validation, and export pipeline. Use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, and record why. GSAP can provide a paused, seekable timeline; mo.js is optional for authored shape and burst accents, not beat analysis. Verify direct and reverse seeks, opening through closing frames, full playback, dimensions, frame rate, sync, and loop continuity.
